Have you ever wondered why the sky is blue during the day but turns orange and red at sunset? It's all about sunlight and the air around us. Sunlight looks white, but it's really made of all the colors of the rainbow mixed together. When that light travels through the atmosphere, it bumps into tiny gas molecules. Blue light gets bounced around a lot more than red light, so blue ends up scattered all across the sky. That's why we see blue when we look up! At sunset, the sun is low on the horizon, and its light has to travel through much more air to reach your eyes. By the time it gets to you, most of the blue has been scattered away, and what's left is the red and orange. So next time you see a glowing sunset, you'll know you're looking at light that's taken the long way around.
